claim: Neotrogla is a Brazilian cave insect belonging to the order Psocodea and family Prionoglarididae.
source: The genus Neotrogla (family Prionoglarididae) is a minute Brazilian cave insect belonging to the order Psocodea (booklice, barklice, and parasitic lice).
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript text describing the taxonomic classification and geographic origin of Neotrogla.

claim: Females of Neotrogla have a penis-like intromittent organ called a gynosome.
source: The females of Neotrogla have a penis-like intromittent organ (gynosome: Figure 1A), which is inserted to a male vagina-like genital cavity for copulation.
evidence: Direct statement supported by reference to Figure 1A showing the gynosome structure.

claim: During mating in Neotrogla, males inject liquid semen into the female's spermatheca through the opening of the spermathecal duct at the tip of the female penis.
source: During mating, the male injects liquid semen into the female's sperm storage organ (spermatheca) through the opening of the spermathcal duct at the tip of the female penis.
evidence: Direct description of the mating process and semen transfer mechanism.

claim: Injected semen induces the formation of a hard capsule shell around itself within the spermatheca.
source: Within the spermatheca, the injected semen then induces the formation of a hard capsule shell around itself (Figure 1A,B: Wearing-Wilde (1995); Yoshizawa et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous work and reference to figures showing the capsule structure.

claim: Two seminal capsules can be attached simultaneously to the spermathecal plate despite there being only a single inlet spermathecal duct.
source: Although there is only a single inlet spermathecal duct present, occasionally two seminal capsules are attached simultaneously to a plate-like structure on the spermatheca (termed 'spermathecal plate': [Lienhard et al., 1893; Yoshizawa et al., 2014]).
evidence: Direct observation reported with supporting citations.

claim: The semen within the capsule is used both for fertilization and consumed by the female as nutrition.
source: The semen within the capsule is used not only for fertilization but is also consumed by the female as nutrition.
evidence: Direct statement about the dual function of the seminal capsule contents.

claim: Sexual selection is reversed in Neotrogla, with females competing for nutritious semen from males.
source: To compete for nutritious semen, the direction of sexual selection is reversed in Neotrogla (sex-role reversal: Yoshizawa et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement about sex-role reversal supported by citation.

claim: Each seminal capsule in Neotrogla has a volume of approximately 0.05 mm³, which corresponds to approximately 300 ml when scaled up to human size.
source: Each seminal capsule is voluminous (~0.05 mm3, corresponding to ~300 ml scaled up to humans)
evidence: Quantitative measurement with scaling comparison provided.

claim: Copulation duration in Neotrogla is very long, lasting 40 to 70 hours.
source: the duration of the copulation is very long (for 40 to 70 hr)
evidence: Direct measurement of copulation duration reported.

claim: In the closely related species Lepinotus patruelis, seminal transfer for forming a similarly voluminous seminal capsule completes in 50 minutes.
source: In a closely related species lacking reversal of genital structure (Lepinotus patruelis, Trogiidae), the seminal transfer for forming a similarly voluminous seminal capsule is known to complete in 50 min (Wearing-Wilde, 1995).
evidence: Comparative data from related species supported by citation.

claim: The female penis of Neotrogla bears many spines that allow females to coercively anchor males during copulation.
source: The female penis of Neotrogla bears a lot of spines, by which females anchor a male coercively during copulation.
evidence: Direct description of morphological feature and its function.

claim: Females are responsible for the very long copulation duration, probably to obtain more semen from males.
source: Therefore, females are obviously responsible for this very long copulation, probably to obtain more semen from a male (Yoshizawa et al., 2014).
evidence: Inference about female control with citation support.

claim: Female Neotrogla frequently have empty capsules within the spermathecal pouch, with up to nine empty capsules and two filled ones observed in an extreme case.
source: Because females frequently have empty capsules within the spermathecal pouch (in an extreme case, up to nine empty capsules and two filled ones attached to the plate were observed: Yoshizawa et al., 2014)
evidence: Observational data with citation support.

claim: Female Neotrogla can be considered polyandrous, which is apparently actively controlled by the female.
source: female Neotrogla can be considered polyandrous, which is apparently controlled actively by the female.
evidence: Inference based on observational data about multiple mating.

claim: Neotrogla is the only example of sex-role reversed animals with a morphological reversal of intromittent organs.
source: Although several examples of sex-role reversed animals induced by seminal gifting have been reported, Neotrogla so far is the only example with a morphological reversal of its intromittent organs (Kamimura and Yoshizawa, 2017).
evidence: Comparative statement supported by citation.

claim: The spermathecal morphology of three examined Neotrogla species (N. brasiliensis, N. aurora, and N. truncata) is practically identical.
source: We examined three species of Neotrogla (N. brasiliensis, N. aurora and N. truncata), the spermathecal morphology of which is practically identical (Lienhard et al., 1893).
evidence: Comparative observation across species with citation.

claim: The spermatheca of Neotrogla is composed of an extensible pouch for storage of the seminal capsule, a spermathecal plate divided into two interconnected sclerites (Sc1 and Sc2), and the spermathecal duct.
source: The spermatheca of Neotrogla is in principle composed of an extensible pouch for storage of the seminal capsule, a spermathecal plate divided into two interconnected sclerites (body sclerites 1 and 2: Sc1 and 2 hereafter), and the spermathecal duct, which discharges into the spermathecal plate (Figure 1CD, Video 1).
evidence: Direct anatomical description supported by figures and video.

claim: Sc2 is a bowl-shaped chitinous structure harboring a fan-like muscle that attaches to a thumb-shaped closure element (CE).
source: Sc 2 is a bowl-shaped chitinous structure harboring a fan-like muscle (the actuator), which originates at its ventral part and attaches to a thumb-shaped controller/closure element (CE: Figures 1CD and 2A–D).
evidence: Anatomical description supported by multiple figures.

claim: The force range of each muscle bundle is between 0.0758–0.6562 mN, assuming a standard intrinsic muscle force of 33 N/cm².
source: Given their attachment area, the force range of each muscle bundle is between 0.0758–0.6562 mN (assuming a standard intrinsic muscle force of 33 N/cm²: David et al., 2016).
evidence: Calculated measurement based on anatomical data and cited standard value.

claim: In virgin females, Sc2 is connected to Sc1 laterally through an interlock-like structure composed of several ridges on both sides that fit into each other.
source: In the virgin female, Sc 2 is connected to Sc 1 laterally through an interlock-like structure composed of several ridges on both sides that fit into each other (Figure 1F).
evidence: Anatomical observation in virgin specimens with figure reference.

claim: The location where Sc1 and Sc2 connect is where seminal capsules are formed during copulation.
source: This is the location where seminal capsules are formed during copulation (Figure 1G).
evidence: Functional observation supported by figure.

claim: Both Sc1 and Sc2 possess a system of patches of resilin, a rubber-like protein found in arthropod cuticles.
source: Both Sc1 and Sc2 possess a system of patches of resilin, a rubber-like protein found in arthropod cuticles wherever potential energy is stored for spring-like motions or bending of structures.
evidence: Anatomical observation with background knowledge about resilin function.

claim: The region surrounding the closure element contains extensive resilin patches.
source: The region surrounding the CE contains extensive resilin patches (Figures 1CD and 2).
evidence: Anatomical observation supported by figures.

claim: Two larger resilin patches are located where the seminal capsules are attached, allowing this region to expand to harbor the base of the seminal capsule.
source: Two larger patches are located where the seminal capsules are attached so that this region can expand to harbor the base of the seminal capsule (Figure 1DF).
evidence: Anatomical observation with functional interpretation supported by figures.

claim: Resilin around the valve mechanism serves to passively keep the valve opening in the closed position.
source: Another resilin-rich region is located around the valve mechanism (Figures 1CD and 2), where the resilin serves to passively keep the valve opening in the closed position.
evidence: Functional interpretation of resilin location supported by figures.

claim: Opening of the valve can only occur through activation of the actuator muscle bundle.
source: Opening of the valve can only occur through activation of the actuator muscle bundle.
evidence: Functional interpretation of the valve mechanism.

claim: In the fixed material analyzed, the muscle bundles are contracted due to the fixation process, resulting in the switching valve being in an opened position.
source: In the fixed material analyzed, the muscle bundles are contracted due to the fixation process. Therefore, the switching valve is in an opened position in Figures 1–2.
evidence: Methodological observation explaining the state of specimens in figures.

claim: The seminal fluid entering the main lumen of the duct can be directed into the left or right channel depending on the position of the closure element.
source: The seminal fluid entering the main lumen of the duct can be directed into the left or right channel depending on the position of the CE.
evidence: Functional description of the valve mechanism.

claim: When the left part of the actuator muscle is activated, the closure element moves to the left, opening a channel on the right side that allows seminal flow into the right capsule.
source: If the left part of the actuator muscle is activated, the CE is moved to the left, so that a channel on the right side opens, which then allows for seminal flow into the right capsule (Figure 2E).
evidence: Functional description of valve operation supported by schematic figure.

claim: A small lateral extension at the distal end of the closure element serves to close the opposite channel during the opening of the other channel.
source: A small lateral extension at the distal end of the CE serves to close the opposite channel during the opening of the other channel (Figure 2DE).
evidence: Anatomical observation with functional interpretation supported by figures.

claim: In a female fixed during copulation, seminal flow from the duct opening lumen toward one of two seminal capsules was clearly observed.
source: In a female fixed during copula, seminal flow from the duct opening lumen toward one of two seminal capsules was clearly observed (Figure 1E).
evidence: Direct observation during copulation supported by figure.

claim: Seminal flow can be directed by the female through differential muscle activation that moves the closure element.
source: Seminal flow can thus be directed by the female through differential muscle activation that moves the CE.
evidence: Functional interpretation based on anatomical and observational data.

claim: Females of Neotrogla use a special mechanism to actively control the direction of seminal flow.
source: The present analyses show that females of Neotrogla use a special mechanism to actively control the direction of seminal flow (Figures 1E and 2A–D).
evidence: Summary statement of findings supported by multiple figures.

claim: The biological switching valve allows females to receive two seminal packages from the same or different males within a short time span.
source: This biological switching valve allows females to receive two seminal packages (i.e., more nutrition) from the same or different males within a short time span.
evidence: Functional interpretation of the valve's adaptive significance.

claim: The switching valve allows females to receive a second seminal capsule while the first one is consumed.
source: In particular, the switching valve allows to receive a second seminal capsule while the first one is consumed.
evidence: Functional interpretation of the valve's adaptive significance.

claim: A similar but less sclerotized structure can be observed in close relatives of Neotrogla (Sensitibilla and Afrotrogla), all belonging to the tribe Sensitibillini.
source: A similar but less sclerotized structure can be observed in close relatives of Neotrogla (Sensitibilla and Afrotrogla, all belonging to the tribe Sensitibillini), suggesting that the structure probably originated in their common ancestor (Lienhard, 1893; Lienhard et al., 1893).
evidence: Comparative observation with evolutionary inference supported by citations.

claim: Neotrogla is distributed in South America, whereas Sensitibilla and Afrotrogla are distributed in southern Africa.
source: Neotrogla is distributed in South America, whereas Sensitibilla and Afrotrogla are distributed in southern Africa.
evidence: Biogeographic information.

claim: The origin of the switching valve dates to at least the break-up of South America and Africa, over 100 million years ago.
source: Therefore, the origin of this switching valve dates to at least the break-up of the two continents, over 100 million years ago (Seton et al., 2012).
evidence: Evolutionary inference based on biogeography and continental drift timing, supported by citation.

claim: In other psocodeans, no sclerite or muscle corresponding to those of the spermathecal plate elements have been observed.
source: In other psocodeans, no sclerite or muscle corresponding to those of the spermathecal plate elements have been observed (Badonnel, 1934; Klier, 1956; Wearing-Wilde, 1995).
evidence: Comparative statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: The spermathecal plate represents an evolutionary novelty.
source: The spermathecal plate thus clearly represents an evolutionary novelty (Müller and Wagner, 2003).
evidence: Evolutionary interpretation supported by citation.

claim: The mechanism of flow control in the biological switching valve is fundamentally different from that in man-made switching valves.
source: The mechanism of flow control and redirection within this biological switching valve is fundamentally different from that in man-made switching valves, which are used, for example in the oil and gas industry.
evidence: Comparative analysis between biological and technical systems.

claim: Technical switching valves use the active rotation of tube or ball elements with various openings to redirect flow, and both closing and opening involve active movement.
source: Technical switching valves use the active rotation of tube or ball elements with various openings to redirect the flow and both closing as well as opening involve an active movement of the valve.
evidence: Description of technical valve mechanisms based on engineering knowledge.

claim: The biological switching valve involves a passive movement component, unlike technical valves.
source: In contrast, the observed biological switching valve involves a passive movement component.
evidence: Comparative statement highlighting difference from technical systems.

claim: The seminal flow is redirected by differential inclination of the closure element due to the fan-like geometry of the actuator muscle working against passive closing forces generated by resilin patches.
source: The seminal flow injected by a male is redirected by a differential inclination of the CE (Figure 2E). This inclination is due to the fan-like geometry of the actuator muscle whose parts can pull the CE in the preferred direction to work against the passive closing forces generated by the resilin patches around the valve complex.
evidence: Functional description of the valve mechanism supported by figure.

claim: The muscle-closure element configuration is advantageous because each muscle bundle pulls in an optimal direction to incline the closure element into one of the two opening positions.
source: This muscle-closure element configuration could be advantageous since each muscle bundle pulls in an optimal direction to incline the CE into one of the two opening positions.
evidence: Functional interpretation of the mechanical advantage of the design.

claim: There is no need for lubrication in the biological valve since the moveable parts do not move against each other.
source: Additionally, there is no need for lubrication since the moveable parts do not move against each other.
evidence: Functional interpretation of the valve design.

claim: Compared to technical switching valves, the biological valve design is advantageous because muscle forces are not redirected via a lever arm.
source: Compared to technical switching valves, this design is advantageous to some extent because the muscle forces are not redirected via a lever arm.
evidence: Comparative analysis of mechanical efficiency.

claim: Female-female competition for males to receive nutritious seminal substances is considered the most important factor driving the evolution of the female penis.
source: Female-female competition for males (sex-role reversal) to receive nutritious seminal substances is considered as the most important factor driving the evolution of the female penis (Yoshizawa et al., 2014).
evidence: Evolutionary interpretation supported by citation.

claim: Among all animals with known sex-role reversal, Neotrogla is the only example in which a female penis evolved.
source: Among all animals with known sex-role reversal, Neotrogla is the only example in which a female penis evolved (Kamimura and Yoshizawa, 2017).
evidence: Comparative statement supported by citation.

claim: In the barklouse species Lepinotus patruelis, a close relative of Neotrogla, sex-roles are reversed but the species possesses normal genital structures.
source: In a close relative of Neotrogla, the barklouse species Lepinotus patruelis (Wearing-Wilde, 1996), the sex-roles are also reversed, but the species possesses normal genital structures.
evidence: Comparative observation supported by citation.

claim: In addition to sex-role reversal, there is at least one other key factor that enabled the evolution of a female penis in Neotrogla.
source: Therefore, it is very likely that, in addition to the sex-role reversal, there is at least one other key factor that enabled the evolution of a female penis.
evidence: Evolutionary inference based on comparative data.

claim: Females of all three known genera of Sensitibillini possess a spermathecal plate.
source: Although females of all three known genera of Sensitibillini possess a spermathecal plate, females of Sensitibilla do not have a penis-like organ (Lienhard, 1893; Lienhard et al., 1893).
evidence: Comparative observation supported by citations.

claim: Females of Sensitibilla do not have a penis-like organ despite possessing a spermathecal plate.
source: Although females of all three known genera of Sensitibillini possess a spermathecal plate, females of Sensitibilla do not have a penis-like organ (Lienhard, 1893; Lienhard et al., 1893).
evidence: Comparative observation supported by citations.

claim: The evolution of the spermathecal plate, possibly including a switching valve, preceded the evolution of the female penis.
source: This strongly suggests that the evolution of the spermathecal plate, possibly including a switching valve, preceded the evolution of the female penis.
evidence: Evolutionary inference based on comparative data.

claim: The spermathecal plate has two slots available for insemination.
source: The spermathcal plate has two slots available for insemination (Figure 1E).
evidence: Anatomical observation supported by figure.

claim: In Neotrogla and Lepinotus, content of the capsule is digested as nutrition during the seminal capsule being attached to the spermathecal plate.
source: In Neotrogla and the related species (Lepinotus), content of the capsule is digested as nutrition during the seminal capsule being attached to the spermathecal plate (the transparent capsule shown in Figure 1B is a digested and empty one: Yoshizawa et al., 2014).
evidence: Functional observation supported by figure and citation.

claim: If there is only one slot for insemination, as in the spermatheca of Lepinotus, females cannot receive another capsule while digesting one.
source: Therefore, if there is only one slot for insemination, as in the spermatheca of Lepinotus, females cannot receive another capsule while digesting one.
evidence: Logical inference based on anatomical constraints.

claim: With the switching valve, female Neotrogla can selectively use one of two slots for insemination while leaving the other slot empty.
source: With the switching valve, the female Neotrogla (and possibly Sensitibilla and Afrotrogla) can selectively use one of two slots for insemination, with leaving the other slot empty.
evidence: Functional interpretation of the valve's adaptive significance.

claim: The switching valve enables females to immediately receive an additional seminal package from the same or other males by using the empty slot.
source: This enables the females to immediately receive an additional seminal package from the same or other males by using the empty slot.
evidence: Functional interpretation of the valve's adaptive significance.

claim: Males are predicted to prudently allocate limited resources to multiple females when operational sex ratio is biased to females.
source: Males are predicted to prudently allocate limited resources, such as nutritious seminal gifts and sperm, to multiple females, especially when operational sex ratio is biased to females, rendering female-female competition for male-derived nuptial gifts (i.e, propensity for multiple mating) more intense (Abe and Kamimura, 2015).
evidence: Theoretical prediction supported by citation.

claim: The male-holding organ (spiny female penis) and female-induced long copulation durations in Neotrogla can be considered as exaggerated adaptations for escalated competition for nuptial gifts.
source: The male-holding organ (spiny female penis) and female-induced long copulation durations of 40 – 70 hr (compared to just ~50 min for formation of one seminal capsule in close relatives) in Neotrogla (Yoshizawa et al., 2014) thus can be considered as exaggerated adaptations for such escalated competition for nuptial gifts in this group of insects inhabiting highly oligotrophic cave habitats (Lienhard and Ferreira, 2013; Lienhard and Ferreira, 2015; Yoshizawa et al., 2014).
evidence: Evolutionary interpretation supported by multiple citations.

claim: Neotrogla inhabits highly oligotrophic (nutrient-poor) cave habitats.
source: in this group of insects inhabiting highly oligotrophic cave habitats (Lienhard and Ferreira, 2013; Lienhard and Ferreira, 2015; Yoshizawa et al., 2014)
evidence: Ecological information supported by citations.

claim: The condition of having two freshly deposited spermatophores at once is comparable to multiple sperm storage organs reported in some animal groups such as dung flies, Drosophila, or tephritid fruit flies.
source: The condition of having two freshly deposited spermatophores at once is comparable to that in multiple sperm storage organs reported for females of some animal groups, such as dung flies, Drosophila, or tephritid fruit flies (Ward, 1993; Pitnick et al., 1999; Twig and Yuval, 2005).
evidence: Comparative statement supported by citations.

claim: Theory predicts that having multiple sperm stores can be a powerful mechanism for choosing sperm.
source: Although theory predicts that having multiple sperm stores can be a powerful mechanism for choosing sperm (Hellriegel and Ward, 1998)
evidence: Theoretical prediction supported by citation.

claim: Evidence is scarce for a gain in fitness by actively selecting for particular sperm from among multiple mates.
source: evidence is scarce for a gain in fitness by actively selecting for particular sperm from among multiple mates (e.g., Demont et al., 2012; Schäfer et al., 2013)
evidence: Summary of empirical evidence supported by citations.

claim: In Neotrogla and Lepinotus patruelis, the content of the seminal capsule is digested quite rapidly if not used for fertilization.
source: In addition, in the case of Neotrogla and related barklice (Lepinotus patruelis), the content of the seminal capsule is digested quite rapidly if not used for fertilization (Wearing-Wilde, 1995; Yoshizawa et al., 2014).
evidence: Observational data supported by citations.

claim: The switching valve system likely represents an adaptation for direct benefits (obtaining more nutrients) rather than for genetic benefits (choosing sperm from high-quality males).
source: Therefore, the switching valve system reported here likely represents an adaptation for direct benefits (i.e., for obtaining more nutrients) rather than for genetic benefits (i.e., for choosing sperm from high-quality males).
evidence: Evolutionary interpretation based on functional and comparative data.

claim: Little interspecific variation in the basic mechanism of the spermathecal plate was detected among the three examined Neotrogla species.
source: Three species of Neotrogla were examined. We detected little interspecific variation in the basic mechanism of the spermathecal plate.
evidence: Summary of comparative observations.

claim: Samples were scanned using synchrotron microcomputed tomography at the BL47XU beamline of SPring-8 using a stable beam energy of 8 keV in absorption-contrast mode.
source: Samples were then scanned using synchrotron microcomputed tomography at the BL47XU (Uesugi and Hoshino, 2012) beamline of the Super Photon ring-8 GeV (SPring-8; Hyogo, Japan) using a stable beam energy of 8 keV in absorption-contrast mode.
evidence: Methodological description with citation.

claim: The tomography system consists of a full-field X-ray microscope with Fresnel zone plate optics.
source: The tomography system consists of a full-field X-ray microscope with Fresnel zone plate optics (Uesugi et al., 2017).
evidence: Methodological description with citation.

claim: The field of view (FOV) and effective pixel size of the tomography system are 0.11 mm² and 0.0826 μm², respectively.
source: The FOV and effective pixel size are 0.11 mm² and 0.0826 μm², respectively.
evidence: Technical specifications of imaging method.

claim: Semiautomatic segmentation algorithms based on gray-value differences in ITK-SNAP were used to obtain 3D representations of the genitalia.
source: We used semiautomatic segmentation algorithms based on gray-value differences in the software ITK-SNAP (Yushkevich et al., 2006) to obtain 3D representations of the genitalia of Neotrogla.
evidence: Methodological description with citation.

claim: For CLSM observation of resilin, an excitation wavelength of 405 nm and an emission wavelength of 420-480 nm were used.
source: To visualize resilin, we used an excitation wavelength of 405 nm and an emission wavelength of 420 – 480 nm, detected on one channel and represented with a blue pseudocolor.
evidence: Methodological description of imaging parameters.
